import "core"


# Tests the syntax view of the debugger: a definition written as intermediate lines leading to a
  result, with a line used twice, a line never used, a nested helper taking its own parameter, an
  [#assert] and a [#debug], a call to another top level function, an if and a bind.
scale(v -> Integer) -> Integer= v * 10

sign(x -> Integer) -> Integer= if(x >= 0)
  Then= 1

  Else= -1

total(a -> Integer, b -> Integer) -> Integer =
  sum= a + b

  unused= a * b

  helper(y -> Integer) -> Integer= y + sum

  #assert(test= sum >= 0)
  #debug(d= sum)
  scale(v= helper(y= sum)) + sum * sign(x= a)

bump(m -> /Data/Maybe[$T -> Integer]) -> /Data/Maybe =
  x<- m

  doubled= x + x

  /Data/Maybe/Some(value= doubled + 1)

main{io -> IO} =
  #assert(test= bump(m= /Data/Maybe/Some(value= 5)) == /Data/Maybe/Some(value= 11))
  io.exit(val= total(a= 1, b= 2) - 63)
